question.worked_solution:
First, we write $1\,\frac{3}{7}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
1\,\frac{3}{7}=\frac{(1\times 7)+3}{7}=\frac{10}{7}
$$

We also write  $4\,\frac{1}{2}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
4\,\frac{1}{2}=\frac{(4\times 2)+1}{2}=\frac{9}{2}
$$

Now, we can multiply the two numbers. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{10}{7}\times \frac{9}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify this product by swapping the denominators:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{10}{7}\times \frac{9}{2} & =\frac{10}{2}\times \frac{9}{7} \\  & =5\times \frac{9}{7} \\  & =\frac{45}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number:

$$
\frac{45}{7}=6\,\text{R}3=6\,\frac{3}{7}
$$
